claim: In patients with diabetic kidney disease and persistent albuminuria, SGLT2 inhibitors significantly reduce the progression of chronic kidney disease and cardiovascular death.
premise: Large-scale clinical trials have demonstrated that sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors significantly reduce the risk of chronic kidney disease progression and cardiovascular death in patients with type 2 diabetes and persistent albuminuria.
section: Diabetic Kidney Disease > SGLT2 Inhibitor Outcomes
evidence_span: SGLT2 inhibitors significantly reduce the risk of chronic kidney disease progression and cardiovascular death in patients with type 2 diabetes and persistent albuminuria.
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: The premise explicitly affirms that SGLT2 inhibitors reduce CKD progression and cardiovascular mortality in patients with diabetic kidney disease and persistent albuminuria.

claim: Renal biopsy is the definitive diagnostic gold standard for establishing the histological subtype and degree of chronicity in lupus nephritis.
premise: Renal biopsy remains the gold standard investigation for establishing the precise histological classification of lupus nephritis (ISN/RPS classes I through VI) and for assessing the activity and chronicity indices that guide immunosuppressive therapy.
evidence_span: Renal biopsy remains the gold standard investigation for establishing the precise histological classification of lupus nephritis
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: The premise directly confirms renal biopsy as the definitive gold standard investigation for histological subtyping and chronicity assessment in lupus nephritis.

claim: Serum potassium concentration greater than 6.5 mmol/L accompanied by electrocardiographic changes requires immediate intravenous calcium gluconate to stabilize the cardiac membrane.
premise: In severe hyperkalemia defined by serum potassium exceeding 6.5 mmol/L or any level with associated ECG changes (such as peaked T waves or widened QRS), urgent administration of 10% intravenous calcium gluconate is indicated to antagonize membrane excitability and stabilize the myocardium.
evidence_span: urgent administration of 10% intravenous calcium gluconate is indicated to antagonize membrane excitability and stabilize the myocardium.
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Directly supported: potassium >6.5 with ECG changes requires urgent IV calcium gluconate for myocardial membrane stabilization.

claim: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease is predominantly caused by pathogenic variants in PKD1 and PKD2 genes.
premise: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is the most prevalent inherited nephropathy, caused by mutations in the PKD1 gene (encoding polycystin-1, accounting for roughly 85% of cases) and PKD2 gene (encoding polycystin-2, accounting for approximately 15% of cases).
evidence_span: caused by mutations in the PKD1 gene... and PKD2 gene
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise explicitly documents that ADPKD is caused by pathogenic variants in PKD1 and PKD2.

claim: Fractional excretion of sodium below 1% strongly suggests a prerenal etiology in oliguric acute kidney injury in the absence of diuretics.
premise: In oliguric patients with acute kidney injury who have not recently received diuretic therapy, a fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa) of less than 1% reflects intact tubular avidity for sodium reabsorption and indicates prerenal azotemia rather than acute tubular necrosis.
evidence_span: fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa) of less than 1% reflects intact tubular avidity... and indicates prerenal azotemia
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: FeNa < 1% in the absence of diuretics indicates prerenal azotemia; fully entailed by premise.

claim: Tolvaptan, a vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist, slows the decline in eGFR and the expansion of total kidney volume in rapidly progressing ADPKD.
premise: Tolvaptan selectively antagonizes vasopressin V2 receptors, thereby inhibiting cyclic AMP-driven cystogenesis. Clinical trials confirmed it significantly slows both total kidney volume enlargement and the rate of eGFR decline in adult ADPKD patients with rapidly progressive disease.
evidence_span: significantly slows both total kidney volume enlargement and the rate of eGFR decline in adult ADPKD patients with rapidly progressive disease.
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Directly entailed: Tolvaptan (V2 antagonist) slows eGFR decline and total kidney volume growth in rapidly progressing ADPKD.

claim: Urine microscopy showing muddy brown granular casts and renal tubular epithelial cells is pathognomonic of acute tubular necrosis.
premise: Centrifuged urine sediment microscopy revealing muddy brown granular casts and sloughed renal tubular epithelial cells provides definitive clinical diagnostic support for acute tubular necrosis (ATN), distinguishing it from prerenal azotemia.
evidence_span: Centrifuged urine sediment microscopy revealing muddy brown granular casts and sloughed renal tubular epithelial cells provides definitive clinical diagnostic support for acute tubular necrosis
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Urinary muddy brown casts and sloughed tubular cells supporting ATN diagnosis is fully supported.

claim: In stage 3b chronic kidney disease, metformin dosage should be adjusted to a maximum of 1000 mg daily with close monitoring of renal function.
premise: For patients with CKD stage 3b (eGFR 30-44 mL/min/1.73m2), the maximum recommended dose of metformin is 1000 mg per day divided into twice-daily dosing, with eGFR monitored at least every 3 to 6 months.
evidence_span: CKD stage 3b (eGFR 30-44 mL/min/1.73m2), the maximum recommended dose of metformin is 1000 mg per day
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Exact stage 3b metformin cutoff of 1000 mg daily is explicitly entailed by the premise.

claim: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs cause prerenal AKI by inhibiting cyclooxygenase-mediated synthesis of vasodilatory prostaglandins in the afferent arteriole.
premise: NSAIDs precipitate acute renal hypoperfusion by inhibiting COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes, impairing the synthesis of renal prostaglandins (PGI2 and PGE2) that are essential for maintaining compensatory afferent arteriolar vasodilation during states of effective volume depletion.
evidence_span: inhibiting COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes, impairing the synthesis of renal prostaglandins (PGI2 and PGE2) that are essential for maintaining compensatory afferent arteriolar vasodilation
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise details the exact biochemical mechanism of NSAID-induced afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction.

claim: Secondary hyperparathyroidism in CKD arises from hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, and decreased synthesis of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.
premise: The pathogenesis of secondary hyperparathyroidism in chronic kidney disease involves a triad of metabolic derangements: phosphate retention causing hyperphosphatemia, reduced renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity leading to calcitriol (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D) deficiency, and systemic hypocalcemia.
section: Mineral and Bone Disorder > Secondary Hyperparathyroidism
evidence_span: triad of metabolic derangements: phosphate retention causing hyperphosphatemia, reduced renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity... and systemic hypocalcemia.
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Triad of hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, and calcitriol deficiency is explicitly stated in premise.

claim: Initial immunosuppressive treatment for minimal change disease in adults is high-dose oral prednisone at 1 mg/kg/day.
premise: First-line induction therapy for minimal change disease presenting with nephrotic syndrome in adults is oral prednisone administered at a dose of 1 mg/kg/day (maximum 80 mg/day) or 2 mg/kg on alternate days for a minimum of 4 weeks.
evidence_span: oral prednisone administered at a dose of 1 mg/kg/day (maximum 80 mg/day) or 2 mg/kg on alternate days for a minimum of 4 weeks.
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Oral prednisone at 1 mg/kg/day as first-line treatment in adults is fully supported.

claim: Anti-glomerular basement membrane disease typically presents with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and alveolar hemorrhage.
premise: Anti-GBM disease (Goodpasture's disease) is characterized clinically by the rapid onset of crescentic glomerulonephritis leading to acute renal failure, frequently accompanied by diffuse pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage manifesting as hemoptysis.
evidence_span: rapid onset of crescentic glomerulonephritis... frequently accompanied by diffuse pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise explicitly documents pulmonary-renal presentation of anti-GBM disease.

claim: In peritoneal dialysis, peritonitis is diagnosed when at least two of the following are present: abdominal pain/cloudy effluent, dialysate leukocyte count > 100/uL with > 50% neutrophils, or positive effluent culture.
premise: Per ISPD guidelines, peritoneal dialysis-related peritonitis requires at least two of three diagnostic criteria: (1) clinical symptoms consistent with peritonitis (e.g., abdominal pain or cloudy peritoneal effluent), (2) effluent leukocyte count > 100/uL with > 50% polymorphonuclear cells, or (3) a positive effluent Gram stain or culture.
evidence_span: requires at least two of three diagnostic criteria: (1) clinical symptoms... (2) effluent leukocyte count > 100/uL with > 50% polymorphonuclear cells, or (3) a positive effluent Gram stain or culture.
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: ISPD 2 of 3 diagnostic criteria explicitly match the claim.

claim: Renal tubular acidosis type 4 is characterized by hyperkalemia and impaired urinary ammonium excretion due to hypoaldosteronism or aldosterone resistance.
premise: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis (hyperkalemic RTA) is distinguished by hyperkalemia out of proportion to the degree of GFR reduction, caused by aldosterone deficiency or tubular resistance to aldosterone, which inhibits renal distal hydrogen and potassium secretion and impairs ammoniagenesis.
evidence_span: distinguished by hyperkalemia... caused by aldosterone deficiency or tubular resistance to aldosterone, which inhibits renal distal hydrogen and potassium secretion and impairs ammoniagenesis.
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Hyperkalemic RTA pathophysiology and features are directly entailed by premise.

claim: Renal ultrasound should be performed within 24 hours in unexplained acute kidney injury to exclude urinary tract obstruction.
premise: In all patients presenting with unexplained acute kidney injury without an obvious prerenal or nephrotoxic etiology, urgent renal ultrasonography is recommended within 24 hours to evaluate for hydronephrosis and exclude post-renal tract obstruction.
evidence_span: urgent renal ultrasonography is recommended within 24 hours to evaluate for hydronephrosis and exclude post-renal tract obstruction.
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Urgent ultrasound within 24h to rule out obstruction in unexplained AKI is directly supported.

claim: ACE inhibitors should be started immediately in all patients with acute kidney injury to preserve long-term renal function.
premise: While ACE inhibitors and ARBs provide established long-term nephroprotection in chronic kidney disease and diabetic proteinuria, they induce efferent arteriolar vasodilation which acutely lowers intraglomerular filtration pressure; consequently, they must be withheld during episodes of acute kidney injury and hypovolemia.
evidence_span: ACE inhibitors and ARBs provide established long-term nephroprotection in chronic kidney disease... consequently, they must be withheld during episodes of acute kidney injury
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: ACE inhibitors protect long-term renal function in CKD, but the claim that they should be started immediately in AKI is contradictory to practice and unsupported in acute states.

claim: KDIGO guidelines recommend target systolic blood pressure below 120 mmHg in all chronic kidney disease patients.
premise: The 2021 KDIGO guideline suggests targeting a systolic blood pressure of < 120 mmHg in adults with chronic kidney disease, but specifically notes that this target applies when using standardized office BP measurement and only in patients not receiving dialysis or kidney transplantation.
evidence_span: targeting a systolic blood pressure of < 120 mmHg in adults with chronic kidney disease... only in patients not receiving dialysis or kidney transplantation.
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Target < 120 mmHg is recommended, but only under standardized measurement and excluding dialysis and transplant patients; claim overgeneralizes to 'all' CKD patients.

claim: Serum creatinine accurately estimates the true glomerular filtration rate in steady-state kidney disease.
premise: Serum creatinine is the most common endogenous biomarker used to calculate estimated GFR (eGFR); however, it is subject to non-renal determinants including muscle mass, dietary meat intake, and tubular secretion, so it only approximates rather than directly measures true GFR.
evidence_span: only approximates rather than directly measures true GFR.
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Creatinine is used to estimate GFR, but it only approximates true GFR due to muscle mass and tubular secretion.

claim: Statin therapy significantly reduces cardiovascular mortality across all stages of chronic kidney disease including dialysis.
premise: Statins significantly reduce cardiovascular events and mortality in non-dialysis CKD stages 1 through 5; however, randomized trials (4D and AURORA) demonstrated that statin initiation does not confer cardiovascular benefit in patients already established on maintenance hemodialysis.
section: Cardiovascular Disease in CKD > Statin Efficacy
evidence_span: Statins significantly reduce cardiovascular events and mortality in non-dialysis CKD... however, randomized trials demonstrated that statin initiation does not confer cardiovascular benefit in patients already established on maintenance hemodialysis.
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Statins reduce CV mortality in non-dialysis CKD, but clinical trials showed no benefit for initiating statins in dialysis patients.

claim: Rituximab is an effective induction therapy for ANCA-associated vasculitis.
premise: Rituximab (anti-CD20) is proven non-inferior to cyclophosphamide for induction of remission in severe ANCA-associated vasculitis, but cyclophosphamide remains the preferred first-line agent in cases of life-threatening crescentic GN with serum creatinine > 500 umol/L or severe alveolar hemorrhage requiring mechanical ventilation.
evidence_span: Rituximab (anti-CD20) is proven non-inferior to cyclophosphamide for induction of remission in severe ANCA-associated vasculitis, but cyclophosphamide remains the preferred first-line agent in cases of life-threatening crescentic GN
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Rituximab is effective and non-inferior, but the premise specifies critical limitations in extreme renal failure/diffuse alveolar hemorrhage.

claim: Intravenous loop diuretics improve survival and reduce the need for renal replacement therapy in acute kidney injury.
premise: Intravenous loop diuretics facilitate volume management and alleviate fluid overload in oliguric acute kidney injury, but rigorous systematic reviews confirm they do not improve patient survival, hasten renal recovery, or decrease the requirement for dialysis.
evidence_span: facilitate volume management... but rigorous systematic reviews confirm they do not improve patient survival, hasten renal recovery, or decrease the requirement for dialysis.
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Diuretics help manage fluid volume in AKI, but evidence confirms they do not improve survival or reduce dialysis need.

claim: All patients with asymptomatic microscopic hematuria should undergo flexible cystoscopy and multiphasic CT urography.
premise: Evaluation of microscopic hematuria involves stratifying patients by age and risk factors for urological malignancy; extensive investigation including cystoscopy and CT urography is recommended for high-risk individuals (e.g. age > 50, smoking history), but is not routinely indicated in low-risk younger patients.
evidence_span: cystoscopy and CT urography is recommended for high-risk individuals... but is not routinely indicated in low-risk younger patients.
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Cystoscopy and CT urography are indicated for hematuria evaluation, but only for risk-stratified high-risk patients, not all patients.

claim: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents should be titrated to normalize hemoglobin levels above 130 g/L in patients with chronic kidney disease anemia.
premise: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) are indicated to alleviate fatigue and reduce transfusion dependence in CKD anemia; however, targeting hemoglobin levels above 115-120 g/L increases the risk of stroke, hypertension, and vascular access thrombosis, so normalization (> 130 g/L) is explicitly discouraged.
evidence_span: ESAs are indicated to alleviate fatigue... however, targeting hemoglobin levels above 115-120 g/L increases the risk of stroke... normalization (> 130 g/L) is explicitly discouraged.
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: ESAs treat anemia in CKD, but targeting hemoglobin >130 g/L is dangerous and discouraged.

claim: Urine dipstick protein reflects total daily urinary protein excretion.
premise: The standard urine dipstick predominantly detects urinary albumin via a colorimetric tetrabromophenol reaction; it is relatively insensitive to low-molecular-weight globulins or Bence Jones proteins and provides only a qualitative estimate influenced by urine concentration.
evidence_span: predominantly detects urinary albumin... relatively insensitive to low-molecular-weight globulins or Bence Jones proteins
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Dipstick detects albumin qualitatively, but misses tubular globulins/Bence-Jones and does not measure total 24h protein.

claim: Renal artery stenting significantly improves blood pressure control and renal survival compared with medical therapy in atherosclerotic renovascular disease.
premise: Large randomized clinical trials (ASTRAL and CORAL) demonstrated that renal artery revascularization with stenting does not confer significant clinical benefit over optimal medical therapy alone regarding blood pressure reduction, preservation of renal function, or prevention of cardiovascular events in atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis.
evidence_span: stenting does not confer significant clinical benefit over optimal medical therapy alone regarding blood pressure reduction, preservation of renal function
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Stenting is a technical option in RAS, but trials (ASTRAL/CORAL) showed no superiority over medical therapy.

claim: Furosemide is effective in managing hypertension in chronic kidney disease patients with normal volume status.
premise: Loop diuretics such as furosemide are potent agents for mobilizing expanded extracellular fluid and controlling volume-dependent hypertension in moderate-to-severe CKD, but their antihypertensive efficacy is limited in patients who are not hypervolemic.
evidence_span: potent agents for mobilizing expanded extracellular fluid and controlling volume-dependent hypertension... efficacy is limited in patients who are not hypervolemic.
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Furosemide treats volume-dependent hypertension in CKD, but has limited efficacy in euvolemic patients.

claim: Plasma exchange is routinely recommended for all patients presenting with ANCA-associated vasculitis.
premise: Plasma exchange has historically been used in ANCA-associated vasculitis; however, the PEXIVAS trial showed that routine plasma exchange does not reduce the long-term incidence of death or end-stage kidney disease, restricting its consideration to select cases with severe diffuse alveolar hemorrhage.
evidence_span: PEXIVAS trial showed that routine plasma exchange does not reduce the long-term incidence of death or end-stage kidney disease
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Plasma exchange is used in select severe pulmonary hemorrhage cases, but routine use in all patients was refuted by PEXIVAS.

claim: Calcium channel blockers provide potent renoprotection by reducing intraglomerular hydraulic pressure.
premise: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers effectively reduce systemic blood pressure in CKD, but cause preferential vasodilation of the afferent arteriole, which can transmit systemic pressures into the glomerulus unless combined with an ACE inhibitor or ARB.
evidence_span: cause preferential vasodilation of the afferent arteriole, which can transmit systemic pressures into the glomerulus unless combined with an ACE inhibitor
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: CCBs reduce systemic BP, but dilate afferent arteriole and do not selectively reduce intraglomerular pressure on their own.

claim: Alport syndrome causes progressive sensorineural hearing loss and ocular abnormalities in all affected family members.
premise: Alport syndrome, most frequently an X-linked dominant condition due to COL4A5 mutations, manifests with progressive glomerulonephritis, high-frequency sensorineural deafness, and anterior lenticonus; however, heterozygous female carriers often exhibit only persistent microscopic hematuria without hearing loss or ocular defects.
section: Collagen IV Disorders > Alport Clinical Spectrum
evidence_span: heterozygous female carriers often exhibit only persistent microscopic hematuria without hearing loss or ocular defects.
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Hearing loss and ocular defects occur in Alport syndrome, but many heterozygous females exhibit only isolated hematuria.

claim: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis responds reliably to alternate-day oral corticosteroid therapy in adults.
premise: Primary FSGS in adults is treated initially with high-dose corticosteroids; however, unlike minimal change disease, complete remission is achieved in only 30% to 50% of patients, with a substantial proportion demonstrating steroid resistance or steroid dependence.
evidence_span: complete remission is achieved in only 30% to 50% of patients, with a substantial proportion demonstrating steroid resistance
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: Corticosteroids are used in adult FSGS, but response is variable (only 30-50% complete remission), not 'reliable'.

claim: Intravenous potassium chloride should be administered as a rapid bolus to treat symptomatic hypokalemia.
premise: Intravenous potassium chloride must always be diluted and administered via controlled infusion at a maximum rate of 10 to 20 mmol/hour under continuous cardiac monitoring. Rapid IV push or bolus of potassium chloride is lethal and strictly contraindicated because it triggers cardiac arrest.
evidence_span: Rapid IV push or bolus of potassium chloride is lethal and strictly contraindicated because it triggers cardiac arrest.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Direct contraindication: IV push potassium is lethal; premise states it must be diluted and infused slowly.

claim: Metformin at 1000 mg twice daily is recommended for glycemic control in patients with end-stage renal disease on maintenance hemodialysis.
premise: Metformin is cleared by the kidneys and accumulates in severe renal impairment, increasing the hazard of fatal lactic acidosis. Metformin is strictly contraindicated in patients with an eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2 and in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis.
section: Pharmacology in Renal Failure > Metformin Contraindications
evidence_span: Metformin is strictly contraindicated in patients with an eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2 and in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Premise explicitly states metformin is strictly contraindicated in ESRD on hemodialysis due to lactic acidosis risk.

claim: Dual therapy combining an ACE inhibitor with an Angiotensin Receptor Blocker is recommended to enhance renal preservation in diabetic nephropathy.
premise: Combination therapy with an ACE inhibitor and an ARB (dual renin-angiotensin blockade) is not recommended because major clinical trials (ONTARGET, VA NEPHRON-D) demonstrated no additional renoprotective benefit but a significantly higher risk of hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury, and cardiovascular events.
evidence_span: Combination therapy with an ACE inhibitor and an ARB... is not recommended... significantly higher risk of hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Dual RAAS blockade is explicitly not recommended due to increased AKI and hyperkalemia risk.

claim: Serum calcium levels are typically elevated in uncomplicated advanced chronic kidney disease prior to treatment.
premise: In untreated advanced chronic kidney disease, impaired renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity reduces calcitriol synthesis and progressive phosphate retention binds free ionized calcium, typically producing systemic hypocalcemia rather than hypercalcemia.
evidence_span: typically producing systemic hypocalcemia rather than hypercalcemia.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Premise directly refutes the claim: untreated advanced CKD produces hypocalcemia, not hypercalcemia.

claim: Bilateral renal artery stenosis is safely managed by initiating high-dose lisinopril and escalating spironolactone.
premise: In bilateral renal artery stenosis (or stenosis in a solitary functioning kidney), glomerular filtration depends critically on angiotensin II-mediated efferent arteriolar vasoconstriction. Initiating ACE inhibitors or ARBs precipitates precipitous drops in GFR and acute renal failure, and is contraindicated.
evidence_span: Initiating ACE inhibitors or ARBs precipitates precipitous drops in GFR and acute renal failure, and is contraindicated.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in bilateral renal artery stenosis because they precipitate acute renal failure.

claim: A 24-hour urine collection with 150 mg of protein per day fulfills the diagnostic criteria for nephrotic-range proteinuria.
premise: Nephrotic-range proteinuria is defined by urinary protein excretion exceeding 3.5 g per 24 hours (or a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio > 3000-3500 mg/g). Daily urinary protein excretion up to 150 mg/day is considered within normal physiological limits.
evidence_span: Nephrotic-range proteinuria is defined by urinary protein excretion exceeding 3.5 g per 24 hours... Daily urinary protein excretion up to 150 mg/day is considered within normal physiological limits.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: 150 mg/day is normal, not nephrotic range (> 3500 mg/day). Severe numeric threshold contradiction.

claim: Prerenal azotemia is typically accompanied by a fractional excretion of sodium exceeding 3%.
premise: Prerenal azotemia is characterized by avid tubular sodium reabsorption resulting in a fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa) < 1% (and fractional excretion of urea < 35%). In contrast, a FeNa > 2% to 3% indicates acute tubular injury where tubular epithelial transport is impaired.
evidence_span: Prerenal azotemia is characterized by avid tubular sodium reabsorption resulting in a fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa) < 1%... In contrast, a FeNa > 2% to 3% indicates acute tubular injury
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: FeNa > 3% contradicts prerenal azotemia (which has FeNa < 1%) and indicates intrinsic acute tubular necrosis.

claim: According to UK NICE guidelines, routine prophylactic antibiotics are recommended for all adult catheterized patients to prevent catheter-associated UTI.
premise: NICE guidelines specifically advise against the routine administration of prophylactic antibiotics in catheterized patients, emphasizing that antibiotics do not prevent catheter-associated bacteriuria but select for multi-drug resistant organisms.
evidence_span: NICE guidelines specifically advise against the routine administration of prophylactic antibiotics in catheterized patients
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Premise explicitly states NICE advises AGAINST routine prophylactic antibiotics in catheterized patients.

claim: Minimal change disease displays extensive subepithelial immune complex deposits on immunofluorescence microscopy.
premise: On immunofluorescence microscopy, minimal change disease is characteristically negative for significant immunoglobulin and complement deposition. Demonstrating extensive subepithelial immune complex deposits is typical of membranous nephropathy, not minimal change disease.
evidence_span: minimal change disease is characteristically negative for significant immunoglobulin and complement deposition.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Minimal change disease has negative immunofluorescence; subepithelial deposits belong to membranous nephropathy.

claim: Potassium-sparing diuretics such as eplerenone should be combined with spironolactone in anuric acute tubular necrosis to promote diuresis.
premise: In anuric patients with acute tubular necrosis, the kidneys cannot excrete filtered potassium. Administering potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g., spironolactone, eplerenone) does not induce diuresis and creates an extreme hazard of fatal hyperkalemia; they must be avoided.
evidence_span: does not induce diuresis and creates an extreme hazard of fatal hyperkalemia; they must be avoided.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Direct contraindication: potassium-sparing diuretics in anuric ATN cause fatal hyperkalemia without diuresis.

claim: Intravenous normal saline is the fluid of choice for correcting severe hypernatremia with free water deficit.
premise: Hypernatremia reflects a deficit of free water relative to body solute. Administering isotonic normal saline (0.9% NaCl) adds sodium and does not correct the free water deficit; the primary replacement fluid is hypotonic fluid such as 5% dextrose in water (D5W) or enteral water.
evidence_span: Administering isotonic normal saline (0.9% NaCl) adds sodium and does not correct the free water deficit; the primary replacement fluid is hypotonic fluid such as 5% dextrose in water
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Normal saline contradicts free water deficit replacement in hypernatremia; hypotonic fluids are indicated.

claim: Serum intact PTH levels should be suppressed to zero in chronic kidney disease patients on dialysis to eliminate bone disease.
premise: Complete suppression of parathyroid hormone (iPTH near zero) leads to adynamic bone disease, an osteomalacic state characterized by profound reduction in bone turnover and increased fracture risk. KDIGO guidelines recommend maintaining iPTH in dialysis patients between 2 and 9 times the upper normal limit.
evidence_span: Complete suppression of parathyroid hormone (iPTH near zero) leads to adynamic bone disease... KDIGO guidelines recommend maintaining iPTH in dialysis patients between 2 and 9 times the upper normal limit.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Premise refutes zero PTH: oversuppression causes adynamic bone disease; target is 2-9x upper normal limit.

claim: Rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia at rates exceeding 20 mmol/L in the first 24 hours prevents neurological injury.
premise: Rapid overcorrection of chronic hyponatremia (> 8-10 mmol/L in 24 hours) precipitates osmotic demyelination syndrome (central pontine myelinolysis), causing irreversible flaccid paralysis, dysarthria, and death. Correction rates must strictly not exceed 8 mmol/L/day.
evidence_span: Rapid overcorrection of chronic hyponatremia (> 8-10 mmol/L in 24 hours) precipitates osmotic demyelination syndrome... Correction rates must strictly not exceed 8 mmol/L/day.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Direct contradiction: correction >20 mmol/L/24h causes fatal osmotic demyelination syndrome.

claim: Hemolytic uremic syndrome is caused by autoantibodies directed against the glomerular basement membrane.
premise: Hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) is a thrombotic microangiopathy characterized by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury, triggered primarily by Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC) or complement regulatory gene defects, not by anti-GBM antibodies.
evidence_span: triggered primarily by Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC) or complement regulatory gene defects, not by anti-GBM antibodies.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Premise directly states HUS is caused by Shiga toxin or complement dysregulation, NOT anti-GBM antibodies.

claim: Loop diuretics act predominantly by inhibiting the sodium-chloride cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule.
premise: Loop diuretics (e.g. furosemide, bumetanide) exert their pharmacological effect by selectively inhibiting the Na-K-2Cl (NKCC2) cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, whereas thiazide diuretics inhibit the Na-Cl cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule.
evidence_span: selectively inhibiting the Na-K-2Cl (NKCC2) cotransporter in the thick ascending limb... whereas thiazide diuretics inhibit the Na-Cl cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: Loop diuretics inhibit NKCC2 in thick ascending limb; distal convoluted tubule Na-Cl cotransporter is the target of thiazides.

claim: Pazopanib improves progression-free survival in metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma compared to sunitinib.
premise: Renal cell carcinoma accounts for roughly 90% of all primary kidney malignancies in adults, with clear cell carcinoma being the most prevalent histological subtype arising from proximal tubular epithelial cells.
evidence_span: Renal cell carcinoma accounts for roughly 90% of all primary kidney malignancies in adults
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: The premise describes RCC epidemiology and histology; it contains zero information about pazopanib or sunitinib oncology trials.

claim: Belatacept provides superior cardiovascular outcomes compared to tacrolimus in kidney transplant recipients.
premise: Maintenance immunosuppressive protocols after renal transplantation frequently include calcineurin inhibitors, antimetabolites, and corticosteroids to prevent acute allograft rejection and prolong graft survival.
evidence_span: Maintenance immunosuppressive protocols after renal transplantation frequently include calcineurin inhibitors
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise lists general immunosuppressive classes, but does not mention or compare belatacept with tacrolimus.

claim: A low-protein diet of 0.55 g/kg/day significantly reduces mortality in non-diabetic CKD stages 4 and 5.
premise: Dietary modification is an integral component of chronic kidney disease care, addressing sodium restriction, potassium management, and phosphorus intake according to individual laboratory parameters.
evidence_span: Dietary modification is an integral component of chronic kidney disease care
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise mentions dietary modification in general, but does not provide evidence on 0.55 g/kg/day protein diet or mortality.

claim: Eculizumab is superior to ravulizumab in preventing relapses of atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome.
premise: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome is an ultra-rare life-threatening thrombotic microangiopathy driven by uncontrolled activation of the alternative complement pathway on endothelial surfaces.
evidence_span: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome is an ultra-rare life-threatening thrombotic microangiopathy driven by uncontrolled activation of the alternative complement pathway
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise describes aHUS complement pathogenesis; no mention or comparative trial data for eculizumab vs ravulizumab.

claim: Screening all healthy adults with routine renal ultrasound reduces the incidence of end-stage kidney disease.
premise: Renal ultrasonography is a safe, non-invasive imaging modality that provides structural assessment of kidney size, cortical thickness, echogenicity, and corticomedullary differentiation without exposing the patient to ionizing radiation or nephrotoxic iodinated contrast.
evidence_span: Renal ultrasonography is a safe, non-invasive imaging modality that provides structural assessment of kidney size
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise describes properties of ultrasound; no evidence supporting population ultrasound screening for ESKD prevention.

claim: Cefepime neurotoxicity in end-stage renal disease is reversed within 2 hours by high-flux hemodialysis.
premise: Cefepime is an antipseudomonal fourth-generation cephalosporin cleared predominantly by renal excretion; neurotoxicity manifesting as encephalopathy or myoclonus has been reported when doses are not appropriately adjusted for reduced kidney function.
evidence_span: Cefepime is an antipseudomonal fourth-generation cephalosporin cleared predominantly by renal excretion
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise reports cefepime neurotoxicity risk in kidney failure, but gives no evidence on hemodialysis clearance timeframes.

claim: Finerenone reduces hospitalizations for heart failure in non-diabetic chronic kidney disease stage 4.
premise: Finerenone is a selective, non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist that provides anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic benefits in clinical trials of chronic kidney disease associated with type 2 diabetes.
evidence_span: selective, non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist that provides anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic benefits in clinical trials of chronic kidney disease associated with type 2 diabetes.
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise describes finerenone in type 2 diabetes CKD; it contains no evidence regarding non-diabetic stage 4 CKD heart failure hospitalizations.

claim: Serum beta-2 microglobulin clearance during online hemodiafiltration is 45% greater than high-flux hemodialysis.
premise: Maintenance hemodialysis utilizes extracorporeal diffusion across a semipermeable membrane to remove water-soluble low-molecular-weight uremic toxins and correct electrolyte and fluid derangements in end-stage renal disease.
evidence_span: utilizes extracorporeal diffusion across a semipermeable membrane to remove water-soluble low-molecular-weight uremic toxins
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise introduces diffusion principles of hemodialysis; does not address convective hemodiafiltration or beta-2 microglobulin clearance numbers.

claim: Patients with IgA nephropathy who carry the HLA-DR4 allele exhibit an 80% lifetime risk of progression to dialysis.
premise: IgA nephropathy is the most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide, characterized immunologically by poorly galactosylated IgA1 producing circulating immune complexes that deposit in the glomerular mesangium.
evidence_span: characterized immunologically by poorly galactosylated IgA1 producing circulating immune complexes that deposit in the glomerular mesangium.
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise explains galactose-deficient IgA1 pathogenesis; HLA-DR4 risk statistics are completely unmentioned.

claim: Adding sodium bicarbonate to preserve residual renal function is indicated when serum bicarbonate is 25 mmol/L in CKD.
premise: Metabolic acidosis in chronic kidney disease develops when the failing kidney cannot excrete daily endogenous fixed acid loads. Sodium bicarbonate supplementation is recommended when serum bicarbonate drops below 22 mmol/L to slow CKD progression and prevent muscle wasting.
evidence_span: Sodium bicarbonate supplementation is recommended when serum bicarbonate drops below 22 mmol/L
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise recommends bicarbonate for levels below 22 mmol/L; serum bicarbonate of 25 mmol/L is normal, and treatment is not supported.

claim: Intravenous iron isomaltoside is superior to ferric carboxymaltose in maintaining transferrin saturation in peritoneal dialysis.
premise: Iron deficiency anemia in chronic kidney disease is assessed by serum ferritin and transferrin saturation (TSAT); intravenous iron preparations are indicated when TSAT is less than 30% and ferritin is less than 500 ug/L.
evidence_span: intravenous iron preparations are indicated when TSAT is less than 30% and ferritin is less than 500 ug/L.
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise outlines iron indication thresholds, but does not compare isomaltoside with ferric carboxymaltose.

claim: Kidney donor profile index below 20% guarantees 25-year graft survival in deceased-donor kidney transplantation.
premise: The Kidney Donor Profile Index (KDPI) combines multiple deceased donor clinical characteristics into a single percentile score to estimate expected allograft longevity, with lower scores indicating longer projected graft survival compared to the broader donor pool.
evidence_span: combines multiple deceased donor clinical characteristics into a single percentile score to estimate expected allograft longevity
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise introduces KDPI as a percentile longevity estimate, but provides no guarantee of 25-year graft survival.

claim: Immediate surgical nephrectomy is the initial management of choice for acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis.
premise: Acute pyelonephritis is an upper urinary tract infection presenting with fever, flank pain, costovertebral angle tenderness, and leukocytosis; initial therapy consists of prompt empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy targeted toward uropathogenic Gram-negative bacilli.
section: Urinary Tract Infections > Acute Pyelonephritis Management
evidence_span: initial therapy consists of prompt empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy targeted toward uropathogenic Gram-negative bacilli.
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise states empiric antibiotics are the initial treatment; surgical nephrectomy for uncomplicated pyelonephritis is unmentioned and medically unsupported.

claim: Cinacalcet increases the risk of symptomatic hypercalcemia in hemodialysis patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism.
premise: Cinacalcet is an oral calcimimetic that increases the sensitivity of the calcium-sensing receptor on the parathyroid gland to extracellular calcium, thereby suppressing parathyroid hormone secretion in patients on dialysis.
evidence_span: increases the sensitivity of the calcium-sensing receptor on the parathyroid gland to extracellular calcium, thereby suppressing parathyroid hormone secretion
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise explains how cinacalcet suppresses PTH; it does not discuss adverse events or hypercalcemia (which in fact calcimimetics lower, not raise).

claim: Membranous nephropathy in children is primarily caused by autoantibodies directed against the PLA2R antigen.
premise: In adults, primary membranous nephropathy is an autoimmune glomerulopathy caused in roughly 70% to 80% of cases by circulating autoantibodies against the M-type phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) expressed on podocyte foot processes.
evidence_span: In adults, primary membranous nephropathy is an autoimmune glomerulopathy caused in roughly 70% to 80% of cases by circulating autoantibodies against the M-type phospholipase A2 receptor
label: NOT_SUPPORTED
rationale: Premise explicitly restricts PLA2R autoantibodies to adults (70-80%); pediatric membranous nephropathy causes are unmentioned.
